meta.theme: ways your memory lies to you
meta.title: 5 ways your memory lies to you

plates.query: Caspar David Friedrich half-hidden landscape in mist painting
faded old painting cracked surface time worn

beats.text: Five unsettling ways your own memory lies to you.
One. You don't replay memories — you rebuild them. And each rebuild quietly edits the original.
Two. Confidence isn't accuracy. The memories you're surest about can be completely wrong.
Three. You keep the peak and the ending, and quietly discard almost everything in between.
Four. Your current mood recolours the past. Sad now, and even good memories turn grey.
Five. With a few suggestions, the mind can build a vivid, detailed memory of something that never happened.
Your past isn't a recording. It's a story you retell — so hold your certainty a little more loosely.
